title: slo-embedded-workstream-sprint-protocol-notes-2026-q3
summary: Working notes describing a lightweight sprint protocol to embed SLO thinking into feature team workstreams. Goal: predictable reliability outcomes without slowing feature delivery — target quick handoffs, measurable experiments, and a reproducible post-release verification checklist.
body:
Context:
We repeatedly see feature launches that ship with partial observability or missing SLOs. This doc defines a pragmatic, team-level sprint protocol so reliability gets embedded into the delivery flow (not an external gating ritual).

Goals:
- Make SLOs part of the sprint lifecycle for any change affecting production surface area.
- Reduce last-minute firefights by surfacing reliability risk earlier.
- Provide a short, actionable checklist that feature teams can run in a single sprint.
- Produce measurable signals (error budget burn rate, latency p95 change, user-impact indicators) within 72 hours of rollout.

Scope:
- Applies to feature work, infra changes, and model rollouts that touch customer-facing endpoints or background pipelines.
- Not intended for minor docs-only PRs or purely exploratory branches.

Principles (keep it lightweight):
1) Default to "observability first": every rollout must include at least one metric and one synthetic check.
2) Small experiments > large one-off migration. Break risky changes into canaries.
3) Ownership is on the feature team; SRE supports and vets, but does not become blocker unless risk is high.

Sprint Protocol (timeline mapped to typical 2-week sprint):
- Sprint week 0 (planning):
  - Feature owner adds an "SLO Impact" section to the ticket: affected routes, expected traffic %, rollout plan (canary thresholds), proposed metrics (latency, error rate, user-facing errors).
  - SRE reviewer assigned if estimated risk > low. If low, feature proceeds with asynchronous review.
  - Add experiment flag or staged rollout plan to the ticket.
- Sprint week 1 (implementation & pre-merge):
  - Instrumentation added: at least one dashboard tile (p95 latency), one counter for user-visible failures, and one synthetic check (end-to-end happy path).
  - Unit and integration tests for observability hooks (smoke).
  - Pre-merge checklist: run local/ci smoke, validate metrics surface in sandbox dashboards.
- Pre-release (24–48h before rollout):
  - Run a readiness sweep with SRE (15-minute sync): confirm dashboards, alert thresholds, rollback plan, and canary duration.
  - Define success criteria for canary and abort thresholds. Document in ticket.
- Rollout (canary stage):
  - Start with small % (configurable by service; default 5%).
  - Monitor defined metrics and synthetic checks. SRE and FE owner watchboard for first 2 hours, async thereafter.
  - Capture any anomalies into the ticket and escalate if thresholds breached.
- Post-rollout (72 hours after full rollout):
  - Run post-release verification checklist (below).
  - Create a short retro note (1–2 paragraphs) summarizing observed vs expected reliability outcomes.

Post-release verification checklist (must be completed and linked in ticket):
- Primary metrics: p95 latency, error rate (5xx/total), user-visible error counter — compare baseline vs post-deploy for 72h window.
- Synthetic checks: green for 72h at configured frequency.
- Logs: sample search for new exception classes or unexpected stack traces.
- Tracing: ensure spans show no large service-to-service latency spikes.
- Incident readiness: on-call pager not engaged during canary. If it was, document root cause.
- Regression protection: quality gates from Redwood Optimize (if configured) passed for model-related changes.

Ownership matrix (simple):
- Feature owner: define SLO impact, add instrumentation, author rollout plan, own post-release retro.
- SRE/embedded partner: vet the plan, assist with dashboards and alerts, act as escalation path during canary.
- Observability infra: ensure synthetic job schedulers and dashboards are provisioned.

Template snippets (to copy into sprint ticket):
- SLO Impact (1–2 sentences): "This change touches /api/generate; expected traffic 12% at peak. Risk to token-generation latency and 500 responses."
- Canary plan: "Start at 5% for 30m, evaluate p95 and error rate; increase 20% every hour if stable; abort if error rate > 0.5% or p95 increases by > 40%"
- Post-release notes: bullet list with metric deltas and short verdict (ok/monitoring/rollback-required).

Measurement and experiments (how we learn):
- For each rollout, capture a small experiment record: metric baseline, canary thresholds, outcome, and one lesson learned. Over 6 sprints we will aggregate to identify common failure modes.
- Suggested queries: a) error budget burn = sum(errors)/expected * 100; b) p95 shift = new_p95/old_p95 - 1; c) user-impact sessions = count(session where error)

Escalation & rollback play (fast path):
- If canary breaches abort thresholds, feature owner triggers config flag to revert and SRE pages on-call.
- Triage within 30 minutes: confirm signal, start rollback, notify stakeholders via #reliability-ops.
- Post-mortem within 72 hours when rollback occurs.

Lightweight runbook links (to include and verify pre-release):
- Service health dashboard templates (CONFLUENCE-5712)
- SLO ownership onboarding checklist (linked artifact above)
- Canary automation playbook (github.com/redwood-inference/canary)
open_questions:
- How to scale this protocol for weekly model micro-rollouts?
- Should we require a quantitative SLO for all model-inference endpoints, or allow qualitative 'monitoring-only' for low-risk variants?
- Can we automate the 24–48h readiness sweep using a checklist bot in Slack?
